record.paper_title: Frequently hypercyclic operators: recent advances and open problems
record.original_question: A frequently hypercyclic subspace for an operator T is an infinite-dimensional closed subspace all of whose nonzero vectors are frequently hypercyclic for T. Characterize the weighted backward shifts B_w on ℓ^p, 1≤p<∞, that possess a frequently hypercyclic subspace. More generally, characterize the operators on separable complex Banach spaces that possess a frequently hypercyclic subspace.

evidence.quote:
Problem 7 (Menet). (a) Characterize the weighted backward shifts Bw on ℓp, 1 ≤ p< ∞ ,
that possess a frequently hypercyclic subspace.
(b) More generally, characterize the operators on a separable ( complex) Banach space

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a separable complex Banach space, and let $T:X\to X$ be a bounded linear operator. A vector $x\in X$ is called frequently hypercyclic for $T$ if for every nonempty open set $U\subseteq X$ the set $\{n\in\mathbb{N}: T^n x\in U\}$ has positive lower density, i.e. $\liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac{1}{N}\#\{1\le n\le N: T^n x\in U\}>0$. A frequently hypercyclic subspace for $T$ is an infinite-dimensional closed linear subspace $M\subseteq X$ such that every nonzero vector of $M$ is frequently hypercyclic for $T$.

For a bounded weight sequence $w=(w_n)_{n\ge 1}$ of nonzero scalars, the weighted backward shift $B_w$ on $\ell^p(\mathbb{N})$, $1\le p<\infty$, is defined by $B_w(x_1,x_2,x_3,\dots)=(w_2 x_2, w_3 x_3, w_4 x_4,\dots)$.

(a) Characterize, in terms of the weight sequence $w$, those weighted backward shifts $B_w$ on $\ell^p$ ($1\le p<\infty$) that possess a frequently hypercyclic subspace.

(b) More generally, give a characterization of those bounded linear operators on a separable complex Banach space that possess a frequently hypercyclic subspace.
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches surface only partial results (sufficient criteria for the existence of frequently hypercyclic subspaces, results for specific classes such as bilateral or weighted shifts), but no complete characterization either for weighted backward shifts on $\ell^p$ or for general operators on separable complex Banach spaces. The characterization problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: A review of some recent work on hypercyclicity
status_evidence.snippet: Survey discusses frequently hypercyclic subspaces and lists characterization as an open direction.
status_evidence.claim: No full characterization is known; surveys list it as open.

status_evidence.title: Difference sets and frequently hypercyclic weighted shifts
status_evidence.snippet: Studies frequently hypercyclic weighted shifts; partial criteria but no full characterization for subspaces.
status_evidence.claim: Existing work provides only partial criteria for frequently hypercyclic weighted shifts.

status_evidence.title: Hypercyclic shifts on lattice graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work continues to develop criteria related to frequent hypercyclicity for shift-type operators.
status_evidence.claim: Research activity continues without a complete characterization of frequently hypercyclic subspaces.
